content.text: No non-compete, field-of-use, territory, or competing-product covenant binding Clear Capital exists anywhere in the agreement. The only Customer-side restraint (p0020) is a licence-scope limit on reselling Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials, which is IP licence scope, not a restriction on the businesses we operate or products we may buy or build — and p0019 confirms the only non-compete-style acknowledgement runs in Contractor's favour.

input.quote: Company may make any changes or additions to the software Consultant created for Company under this Agreement, which Company in Company's discretion may consider necessary, and Company may engage others to make any such changes or additions, without further payments to Consultant.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no non-compete, competing-product, field-of-use, or territory restriction on Clear Capital. Section 1 (Purpose of Engagement), the Term, Termination, warranty and liability sections contain no restrictive covenant, and targeted searches for compete/exclusivity/"Company shall not"/solicitation language return nothing responsive. The only Customer-side restraint is in § 4(b)(ii) ("Company shall not resell or make use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives under this Agreement"), which is a licence-scope limitation on Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials rather than a limit on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build; § 4(c) separately grants us a perpetual licence for "Company's business operations" and § 4(d) expressly lets us engage others to modify the software. The § 4(b) preamble non-compete-style acknowledgement runs in Contractor's favour (Contractor may serve other clients), which does not bind us. This sits at the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.
